objectives:
This seminar, joined by visiting professor Jason McGrath, is designed as a career retrospective study of the cinema of Hou Hsiao-hsien 侯孝賢 and an exploration of the broader phenomenon that he helped to inspire, variously known as “Asian minimalism,” “Asian slow cinema,” or, in this course, “Asian long-take cinema.” The seminar will trace the development of Hou’s distinctive style from his early films through his classics of “Taiwan New Cinema”台灣新電影 in the mid/late 1980s, and on to his later films when he had become an internationally celebrated auteur even after the Taiwan-specific movement he had been part of had died out. We will particularly focus on his use of long-take and long-shot cinematography and explore how that style has been theorized by film scholars and critics since the classical film theory of André Bazin.

Hou’s stylistic connections to other Asian filmmakers will be explored in the course first by a look back at the cinema of Ozu Yasujiro 小津 安二郎and then later in the course with weeks devoted to the films of Tsai Ming-liang 蔡明亮 (Taiwan), Jia Zhangke 賈樟柯 (mainland China), Apichatpong Weerasethakul (Thailand), Bi Gan 畢贛 (mainland China), and Phạm Thiên Ân (Vietnam). These comparative studies will both provide observations of the influence of Hou on other directors of East and Southeast Asia and suggest the ways that long-take aesthetics in cinema has been taken in new directions in recent years.

Students will be evaluated on their contributions to course discussions and on short written responses, culminating in a final paper on a topic that will also be presented in class during the final week of the course.

Learning Objectives:

For the purpose of education at the Master’s degree level as well as the upper-division (advanced) undergraduate level, this course serves two main objectives:
1.	Provide an in-depth, comprehensive exploration of the cinema of Hou Hsiao-hsien as an exemplary Taiwan filmmaker who both pioneered new stylistic directions in the art of cinema and documented the rich history, culture, and society of Taiwan.
2.	Serve as a detailed exploration of film aesthetics, with a particular focus on the long-take style and its relationship to larger questions of cinematic realism. This style had roots in certain directors of French “poetic realism,” a few Hollywood auteurs such as Orson Welles, and particularly Italian Neorealism, but it has reached new extremes in recent decades, partly enabled by the shift from celluloid film to digital cinema, and Asian filmmakers have been at the forefront of experimentation with the style.
content:
WEEK 1
Film:
《風櫃來的人》 The Boys From Fengkuei (HHH, 1983)
Readings:
André Bazin, “The Evolution of Film Language” in Bazin, What Is Cinema?, trans. Timothy Barnard (Montreal: Caboose, 2009), 87–106.

WEEK 2
Films:
《就是溜溜的她》 Cute Girl (HHH, 1980)
《風兒踢踏踩》 Cheerful Wind (HHH, 1981)
《在那河畔青草青》 The Green, Green Grass of Home (HHH, 1982)
Readings:
林文淇：〈侯孝賢早期電影中的寫實風格與敘事〉，收入林文淇、沈曉茵、李振亞編：《戲戀人生：侯孝賢電影研究》（台北：麥田出版有限公司，2000年），頁93-111。

WEEK 3
Films:
《兒子的大玩偶》His Son’s Big Doll (HHH, 1983)
《冬冬的假期》 A Summer At Grandpa’s (HHH, 1984)
Reading:
Huang Chunming 黃春明, 《兒子的大玩偶》“His Son’s Big Doll”
Christopher Lupke, ch 1 “The Odyssey of Hou Hsiao-hsien” & ch 2 “Zhu Tianwen and the Sotto Voce of Gendered Expression,” in Lupke, The Sinophone Cinema of Hou Hsiao-hsien (Cambria, 2016), 1-76.

WEEK 4
Films:
《童年往事》 A Time To Live, A Time To Die (HHH, 1985)
《戀戀風塵》 Dust In The Wind (HHH, 1986)
Reading:
Haden Guest,  “Reflections on the Screen: Hou Hsiao Hsien’s Dust in the Wind and the Rhythms of the Taiwan New Cinema, ” in Island on the Edge: Taiwan New Cinema and After,  ed. Chris Berry and Feii Lu (Hong Kong University Press,  2005),  27-38.
Steve Neale, “Introduction 2: The Long Take—Concepts, Practices, Technologies, and Histories,” in The Long Take: Critical Approaches, ed. by John Gibbs and Douglas Pye (Palgrave Macmillan, 2017), 27-41.

WEEK 5
Films:
《尼羅河女兒》 Daughter of The Nile (HHH, 1987)
《千禧曼波》 Millennium Mambo (HHH, 2001)
Reading:
Jason McGrath “Daughter of the Nile (1987): Hou Hsiao-hsien’s Dark Pop Experiment,” in 32 New Takes on Taiwan Cinema, edited by Emily Yueh-yu Yeh, Darrell William Davis, and Wenchi Lin (University of Michigan Press, 2022), 176-90.
鄭美里：〈看得見與看不見的城市：：《尼羅河女兒》、《千禧曼波》中的空間與性別〉，收入林文淇、沈曉茵、李振亞編：《戲戀人生：侯孝賢電影研究》（台北：國家電影中心，2014年），頁98-109。
Christopher Lupke, ch 5 “Time and Teleology in Hou Hsiao-hsien’s Films of Quest and Disillusionment,” in Lupke, The Sinophone Cinema of Hou Hsiao-hsien (Cambria, 2016), 153-208.

WEEK 6
Film:
《悲情城市》 A City of Sadness (HHH, 1989)
Reading:
林文淇：〈「回歸」、「祖國」與「二二八」：《悲情城市》中的台灣歷史與國家屬性〉，收入林文淇、沈曉茵、李振亞編：《侯孝賢電影的城市、歷史，美學》（台北：麥田出版有限公司，2000年），頁157-180。
Markus Nornes, “Hou Hsiao-hsien and Narrative Space,” in Hou Hsiao-hsien, ed. Richard Suchenski (Vienna: Österreichisches Filmmuseum and New York: Columbia University Press, 2014), 154-168.
Rawnsley, Ming-yeh. T. “Cinema, Historiography, and Identities in Taiwan: Hou Hsiao-hsien’s A City of Sadness.” Asian Cinema 22, 2 (2011): 196–213.
Shie, Elliott Shir-Tzung. “Politics, Lyricism and A City of Sadness: Towards a Critique of the Chinese Lyrical Tradition in Taiwan.” Asian Cinema 35, nos. 1/2 (2025): 81-98.

WEEK 7
Films:
《戲夢人生》 The Puppetmaster (HHH, 1993)
《好男好女》 Good Men, Good Women (HHH, 1995)
Reading:
Jean Ma, ch 1 “Time without Measure, Sadness without Cure,” in Ma, Melancholy Drift: Marking Time in Chinese Cinema (Hong Kong University Press, 2010), 19-50.
James Udden, “Hou Hsiao-hsien and the Question of a Chinese Style.” Asian Cinema 13, 2 (Fall/Winter 2002): 54-75.
James Udden, “‘This Time He Moves’: The Deeper Significance of Hou Hsiao-hsien’s Radical Break in Good Men, Good Women,” in Cinema Taiwan: Politics, Popularity and State of the Arts, ed. Darrell William Davis and Ru-Shou Robert Chen (Routledge, 2007), 183-202.

WEEK 8
Films:
《南國再見，南國》 Goodbye South, Goodbye (HHH, 1996)
《海上花》 Flowers of Shanghai (HHH, 1998)
Reading:
Shiao-Ying Shen, “Goodbye South, Goodbye (1996): Another Gangster Movie?” in 32 New Takes on Taiwan Cinema, edited by Emily Yueh-yu Yeh, Darrell William Davis, and Wenchi Lin (University of Michigan Press, 2022), 231-243.
葉月瑜：〈侯孝賢電影詩學：《海上花》〉，收入林文淇、沈曉茵、李振亞編：《戲戀人生：侯孝賢電影研究》（台北：麥田出版有限公司，2000年），頁337-350。
Laura Feijó, “Between Unity and Fragmentation: The Highly Choreographed Long Take,” Screen 65, no. 4 (Winter 2024): 530-553.

WEEK 9
Films:
《珈琲時光》 Café Lumiere (HHH, 2003)
《東京物語》 Tokyo Story (Ozu Yasujiro 小津 安二郎, 1953)
Reading:
吳怡芬(I-fen Wu), The Poetics of Asian Minimalism: Long Take/Long Shot Stylistics in the Films of Ozu Yasujiro, Hou Hsiao-Hsien and Kore-eda Hirokazu, 中央大學藝術學研究所, 藝術學研究, 2017-12 (21), 209-237.
Christopher Lupke, ch 3 “Comparing Hou Hsiao-hsien and Ozu Yasujirô,” in Lupke, The Sinophone Cinema of Hou Hsiao-hsien (Cambria, 2016), 77-112.
I-fen Wu, “Remapping Ozu’s Tokyo? The Interplay between History and Memory in Hou Hsiao-hsien’s Cafe Lumiere,” Asian Cinema 19, no. 1 (Spring/Summer 2008): 172-81.

WEEK 10
Films:
《不散》 Goodbye, Dragon Inn (Tsai Ming-liang 蔡明亮, 2003)
《郊遊》 Stray Dogs (Tsai Ming-liang 蔡明亮, 2013)
Reading:
Lutz Koepnick, ch 7 “(Un)timely Meditations” in Koepnick, The Long Take: Art Cinema and the Wondrous (University of Minnesota Press, 2017), 181-221.
Tiago de Luca, “Watching Cinema Disappear: Intermediality and Aesthetic Experience in Tsai Ming-liang’s Goodbye Dragon Inn (2003) and Stray Dogs (2013),” in The Long Take: Critical Approaches, ed. by John Gibbs and Douglas Pye (Palgrave Macmillan, 2017), 163-176.

WEEK 11
Films:
《最好的時光》 Three Times (HHH, 2005)
《紅氣球》 The Little Red Balloon (HHH, 2007)
Reading:
Wenchi Lin, “Three Times (2005): Hou Hsiao-hsien’s Cinematic Poetics of Mise-en-Song,” in 32 New Takes on Taiwan Cinema, edited by Emily Yueh-yu Yeh, Darrell William Davis, and Wenchi Lin (University of Michigan Press, 2022), 286-300.
Dag Sodtholt, “The Complexity of Minimalism: Hou Hsiao-hsien’s Three Times,” Senses of Cinema 39 (April-June 2006), https://www.sensesofcinema.com/2006/spotlight-on-hou-hsiao-hsien/three_times/.
謝世宗 (Elliott Shr-tzung Shie)：〈跨國電影、觀光客的凝視與抒情在他方〉，《侯孝賢的凝視：抒情傳統、文本互涉與文化政治》（新北市：群學，2021年），頁255-295。

WEEK 12
Film:
《刺客聶隱娘》 The Assassin (HHH, 2015)
Reading:
Hsiu-Chuang Deppman, “Ethics and Aesthetics in The Assassin,” in The Assassin: Hou Hsiao-hsien’s World of Tang China, ed. Peng Hsiao-yen (Hong Kong University Press, 2019), 161-177.
Andrew Stuckey, “The Restrained Fantastic in Hou Hsiao-hsien’s The Assassin” in Sino-Enchantment: The Fantastic in Contemporary Chinese Cinemas, ed. Kenneth Chan and Andrew Stuckey (Edinburgh University Press, 2021), 95-111.
Ziru Chen, “Hou Hsiao-hsien’s Departure from Language in His Postmillennial Films,” Modern Chinese Literature and Culture 37 no. 1 (June 2025): p.90-123.

WEEK 13
Films:
《小武》Xiao Wu (aka Pickpocket; Jia Zhangke 賈樟柯, 1997)
《站台》Platform (Jia Zhangke 賈樟柯, 2000)
Reading:
Jia Zhang-ke, “A Bard Singing the Remembrances of a Nation,” in Hou Hsiao-hsien, ed. Richard I. Suchenski (Synema, 2014), 182-84.
Jason McGrath, “The Independent Cinema of Jia Zhangke: From Postsocialist Realism to a Transnational Aesthetic” in The Urban Generation: Chinese Cinema and Society at the Turn of the Twenty-first Century, ed. Zhang Zhen (Duke University Press, 2007), 81-114.

WEEK 14
Films:
Syndromes and a Century (Apichatpong Weerasethakul, 206)
Uncle Boonmee Who Can Recall His Past Lives (Apichatpong Weerasethakul, 2010)
Reading:
Ari Purnama, “Syndromes of Indirect Communication: A Functional Analysis of the Static Long-take Technique in Apichatpong Weerasethakul’s Feature Films,” Asian Cinema 26, no. 2 (2015): 205-222.
Palita Chunsaengchan, “The critique of Anticommunist State Violence in Uncle Boonmee Who Can Recall His Past Lives,” Asian Cinema 32, no. 1 (April 2021): 95-111.

WEEK 15
Films:
《路邊野餐》Kaili Blues (dir. Bi Gan 畢贛, 2015)
Inside the Yellow Cocoon Shell (Phạm Thiên Ân, 2023, 179 min)
Reading:
Lutz Koepnick, “Introduction” & ch 3 “It’s Still Not Over” in Koepnick, The Long Take: Art Cinema and the Wondrous (University of Minnesota Press, 2017), 1-32, 78-112.

WEEK 16
Student Presentations of Final Paper topics
books: 主題相關之專書章節與期刊論文

每週閱讀／觀影心得 30％
課堂報告 20％
期末論文 50％
